title: Taking an AI-assisted alchemy game from repeated iterations to Google Play review
author: Aether_Ash_Forge
selftext:
My Android game, Aether & Ash Forge: Alchemy, is currently in Google Play review. I wanted to share some of the process behind it rather than just drop a trailer.



I’ve used AI assistance for code and some artwork, while directing the game’s design, presentation, and release decisions. The work has involved repeated revisions: reviewing visual concepts, choosing a direction, checking the implementation, and refining what actually appears in the game.



One important part has been protecting player progress. Changes have gone through save-protection checks and in-place phone updates, checking that the existing Journal and settings survive installation, launch, backgrounding, and restart.



The game itself is about mixing ingredients, discovering essences, crafting medieval weapons, and uncovering a story through quests.



Gameplay and screenshots: [https://aetherashforge.com](https://aetherashforge.com)



There’s no confirmed launch date yet. For others using AI to build games, what has been your most useful check for catching regressions between iterations?
